title: When AI Breaks Your Assignments
author: Patrick Dempsey
summary: AI language models fundamentally alter classroom assignment design by making traditional essay and analysis prompts solvable by machines. Teachers must redesign assessments to remain meaningful in an AI world, shifting from assignments optimized for human effort to assignments that require student judgment, synthesis, and application. The problem isn't that students can use AI—it's that teachers designed assignments assuming AI wouldn't exist. This challenge forces reconsideration of what learning actually requires and which assignments genuinely assess understanding versus which merely consume time.
points: AI capability doesn't break assignments—poor assignment design does
Teachers must redesign assessments around what AI cannot do: authentic judgment and synthesis
Traditional essay assignments assuming AI won't help become obsolete overnight
The AI challenge forces clarity about what learning truly requires versus what mimics it
Assignment design in 2026 requires either human judgment tasks or AI-resistant assessments
quotes: AI doesn't break assignments. It exposes which assignments were never about learning.
When students can pass your assignment by using AI, your assignment was testing effort, not understanding.
Assignment design in the AI era requires fundamentally rethinking what learning actually looks like.
Essays that AI can generate perfectly aren't broken by AI—they were never strong assessment.
The real work is designing tasks that require human thinking AI cannot replicate.
